subject.title: Allow before_agent_start hooks to override prompt

question: Should OpenClaw add a user-prompt replacement contract for plugins, and should it live on before_prompt_build with legacy before_agent_start compatibility or on a broader llm_input interception hook?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the permanent API shape controls plugin compatibility and a security-sensitive prompt mutation boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Add prompt-build replacement contract
options.body: Extend before_prompt_build as the canonical plugin API, optionally bridge legacy before_agent_start, and enforce allowPromptInjection and precedence across all runners.

options.title: Use broader LLM interception
options.body: Resolve this through the llm_input/llm_output modifying hook direction and keep before_prompt_build additive-only.

options.title: Reject prompt replacement
options.body: Keep plugins limited to additive context/system prompt changes and document that full prompt replacement is intentionally unsupported.

recommendation.title: Add prompt-build replacement contract
recommendation.body: Extend before_prompt_build as the canonical plugin API, optionally bridge legacy before_agent_start, and enforce allowPromptInjection and precedence across all runners.

likelyOwner.reason: They recently worked on the hook contract split and Codex prompt hook parity, making them the strongest routing owner for this API choice.
